claim.expected_behavior: Given one of these abbreviations, the skill returns the corresponding full monosaccharide name as tabulated.
claim.scope: IUPAC condensed / standard glycan monosaccharide symbol-to-name mapping as used in glycan notation.
claim.statement: The skill's IUPAC condensed monosaccharide abbreviations are: Neu5Ac = N-acetylneuraminic acid (sialic acid), GlcNAc = N-acetylglucosamine, GalNAc = N-acetylgalactosamine, Man = mannose and Fuc = fucose.

limitations:
What the cited evidence covers. KEGG COMPOUND C00270 lists Neu5Ac among the names of N-Acetylneuraminate / N-Acetylneuraminic acid, and its BRITE hierarchy names entry C00270 as N-Acetylneuraminic acid, supporting the claim's mapping Neu5Ac = N-acetylneuraminic acid. KEGG C00140 lists GlcNAc among the names of N-Acetyl-D-glucosamine, supporting GlcNAc = N-acetylglucosamine. The ChEBI record for CHEBI:28037 carries the label N-acetyl-D-galactosamine with GalNAc and D-GalNAc as synonyms, and KEGG C01132 names the same compound, supporting GalNAc = N-acetylgalactosamine. The ChEBI fucose record (CHEBI:2181, L-fucopyranose) gives 6-deoxy-L-galactose / 6-deoxy-L-galactopyranose, which supports the skill's classification of fucose as a deoxyhexose.

What the cited evidence does not cover. (1) The abbreviation Man for mannose is asserted by the claim but no retrieved reference in this claim's evidence states it; neither KEGG nor the ChEBI records retrieved here list Man as a synonym. (2) The abbreviation Fuc for fucose is likewise not stated in the retrieved ChEBI fucose record; only the full name and the 6-deoxy relationship are. (3) The parenthetical '(Sialic acid)' for Neu5Ac is not stated in the retrieved records: KEGG classifies Neu5Ac under Carbohydrates / Monosaccharides / Amino sugars, not under a 'sialic acid' label. (4) The claim's 'Type' column values (Hexose, HexNAc, Sialic acid) are glycobiology class labels that these chemical databases express differently (amino sugars, deoxyhexose), so the type assignments are only partly corroborated. (5) No case-based execution evidence exists for this claim: the subject skill was never run for it, so this assessment speaks only to documentary consistency between the claim and the cited sources, not to the skill's behaviour.

Why this is the documentary path. The independent grade-critique session required before any A-to-C execution grade failed three separate times in this run (recorded by the runtime as critic_response_invalid) for three other claims, across three different designs and two levels of justification verbosity, so no execution grade was reachable in this environment. This claim's catalog lookup was performed, none of the four candidates already in the catalog matches this claim's nomenclature scope, and no candidate was qualified for this claim, so nothing qualified has been left unexecuted. All six quotes above are from bytes Python itself retrieved over public HTTPS from KEGG REST and the EMBL-EBI Ontology Lookup Service. One further reference retrieved for this claim (Essentials of Glycobiology chapter 1, NCBI Bookshelf NBK579927) is pinned in the run but was too large to be displayed to the planner, so nothing is quoted from it.
